message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA; one is explicitly prevalent). Several come from pan-trait/framework contexts (PGS001784: Global Biobank framework; PGS002054: UKB portability framework), which domain guidance says should generally be down-ranked when disease-focused multi-cohort AAA models exist. Among the disease-focused options, the Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis family (PGS003972/PGS003973) provides coherent, multi-cohort development and direct AAA endpoints; however, both mainly report full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.69 for PGS003972; C-index 0.882 for PGS003973) without explicit PRS-only AUROC, limiting cross-model comparability. PGS003972 is selected over PGS003973 because its reported metric is an AUROC (more directly comparable across classifiers than a C-index here) and both have similar endpoint alignment and multi-cohort context, but the lack of PRS-only/incremental metrics and ambiguity about covariate handling in some competitors keep this from being a clearly high-quality, conflict-free choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have acceptable endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is AAA for all; PGS000753 is prevalent AAA but still a direct diagnosis endpoint). Evidence is mixed and not cleanly comparable across candidates: several report only full-model AUROC/C-index (PGS001784 AUROC=0.868; PGS003973 C-index=0.882; PGS003429 AUROC=0.708; PGS003972 AUROC=0.69) with varying/unknown covariates, and domain guidance cautions against treating full-model discrimination as PRS-only evidence. PGS000753 provides a PRS-relevant effect size (OR per SD 1.37, CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) and a disease-focused publication context, making it the most interpretable standalone-PRS signal among the available options. However, confidence is limited because stronger-looking full-model metrics exist in other candidates but cannot be fairly compared (covariates unknown or not PRS-only), and some candidates have much larger validation samples (e.g., PGS001784 n=350,767) or are from broader framework/portability studies (PGS001784, PGS002054), leaving unresolved uncertainty about which score best captures PRS-only discrimination."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (no horizon-conditioned risk packaging). Among them, PGS000753 is from a disease-focused abdominal aortic aneurysm genetic architecture study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and reports a relatively strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with multi-ancestry evaluation noted (AFR/EUR), supporting PRS signal without obvious covariate inflation. Competing candidates include framework/portability-style scores (PGS001784 from a global biobank methods paper; PGS002054 from a UKB portability paper) and newer disease-focused PRS-CS scores (PGS003972/PGS003973) that report only full-model AUROC/C-index without PRS-only metrics and have unknown/limited covariate detail, making cross-model comparability difficult; PGS003429 is a screening cost-effectiveness paper and also only reports full-model metrics with unknown covariates. Overall, missing PRS-only AUC/R2 for most disease-focused candidates and reliance on non-comparable full-model metrics (some with high values likely driven by age/sex) prevent a clearly high-quality single best choice from the visible evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype endpoints aligned to abdominal aortic aneurysm (one explicitly prevalent AAA). However, the strongest-looking discrimination values in the set are full-model metrics (e.g., AUROC=0.868 in PGS001784 and C-index=0.882 in PGS003973) rather than clearly isolated PRS-only metrics, so they are not directly comparable as PRS quality signals per the provided domain guidance; additionally, some of these come from framework-style papers (Global Biobank analyses; UKB portability), which the guidance recommends down-ranking when disease-focused alternatives exist. PGS000753 is from a disease-focused AAA study (Million Veteran Program AAA genetics paper) with clean/basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and reports an interpretable per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) in European validation, making it a coherent, endpoint-faithful choice without relying on potentially covariate-driven full-model AUROC. Remaining limitation: PGS000753 lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2, and several newer multi-cohort PRS-CS/shaPRS candidates exist but also report only full-model metrics with unknown or limited covariate detail, leaving residual uncertainty and preventing a high-confidence ‘best’ selection."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm), so the decision hinges on study archetype, comparability of performance evidence, and validation support. PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet, multi-cohort list including MVP, HUNT, deCODE, UKB, etc.), which the provided domain policy indicates should generally be preferred over portability/framework-derived scores when endpoints are equally aligned. Between these two siblings, PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) but with only basic covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex); however, because this is not a clearly PRS-only metric, it is less comparable for PRS ranking, and PGS003972 has more validation records (record_count=3 vs 1), suggesting broader reported evaluation support within the same disease-focused family. Competing models PGS002054 (UKB portability paper) and PGS001784 (Global Biobank framework) have explicit PRS-only/PRS-comparable R2 (~0.014–0.015), but the domain guidance discourages letting framework scores win solely on metric availability when a disease-focused multi-cohort AAA score exists. Therefore PGS003972 is selected as the best-supported direct-match candidate, with Moderate confidence due to reliance on full-model metrics (AUC/C-index) and limited PRS-only metrics across the disease-focused candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with aligned trait_reported/trait_efo and diagnosis-style phenotyping_reported (one is explicitly prevalent AAA). However, the evidence is not strong enough to declare a single clearly best model because most candidates lack PRS-comparable metrics (top-level PRS-only AUROC/R2 are largely null) and several report only full-model discrimination. Among the set, PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused, multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis context (Nat Genet AAA loci paper; many contributing cohorts listed) with a modern genome-wide method (PRS-CS) and direct AAA phenotype, making it less framework-like than the UKB portability score (PGS002054) and the Global Biobank cross-trait framework score (PGS001784). The main limitation is that PGS003972’s reported AUROC=0.69 appears to be a full-model metric with unknown covariates and no PRS-only/incremental metric, while PGS003973 reports a higher C-index (0.882) but also reflects covariate-included prediction (Age/Age^2/Sex) rather than isolated PRS performance; without comparable PRS-only metrics across these siblings, the selection remains uncertain."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype-aligned endpoints (mostly “Abdominal aortic aneurysm”; PGS000753 is “Prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm,” which is still a direct disease endpoint). However, the performance evidence is not cleanly comparable across candidates: several report only full-model AUROC/C-index (PGS001784, PGS003429, PGS003972, PGS003973) without a clearly PRS-only AUROC; PGS002054 reports partial-r; and PGS000753 reports only an OR per SD (1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44). Following the domain guidance to avoid over-weighting full-model discrimination and to prefer disease-focused studies over pan-trait/portability frameworks, PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused abdominal aortic aneurysm genetic-architecture study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) with basic covariate adjustment (age/sex/PCs) and multi-ancestry evaluation. The main limitation is that it lacks explicit PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (AUC/R2), while some framework-style alternatives provide PRS-only R2 or very high full-model AUROC/C-index that may be largely covariate-driven; this keeps confidence below high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype strings consistent with AAA. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo align to abdominal aortic aneurysm, and phenotyping_reported is AAA or prevalent AAA). Confidence is moderated because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/incremental AUROC) are missing for the disease-focused models, and the framework models provide PRS-only R2/partial-r that are small and not directly comparable to full-model discrimination."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004561","confidence":"Low","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS004491 and PGS004561), both aligned to the target via trait_efo=acute kidney injury and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported=N17 (Acute renal failure), and both come from the same publication, same UKB training cohort (n=174,489), same EUR-only development/evaluation, same validation sample size (n=56,192), and both have missing PRS-comparable performance metrics (AUC/R2 all null) with covariates listed as Unknown—so endpoint fidelity is good but comparative evidence is limited. {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are concept-level direct matches via trait_efo=age-related macular degeneration, but they differ in endpoint fidelity, study archetype, and the interpretability/comparability of reported metrics. PGS004606 has the cleanest phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Age-related macular degeneration) and comes from a disease-focused AMD genetics paper (Nat Genet) with large European evaluation support (n=163,011) and only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1–10).
